Lemma
[The New Vector is Orthogonal to its Predecessors]

↗ def:gram-schmidt-bilin

Let $u=\mathrm{GS}_B(v)$ and $j=k+1$. Suppose \[ B(u_i,u_i) e 0\quad (i\leq k), \qquad B(u_i,u_{i'})=0\quad (i e i',\ i,i'\leq k). \] Then $B(u_c,u_j)=0$ for every $c<j$.

Proof

↗ def:gram-schmidt-bilin \sketch Expanding the recursion gives

\[ B(u_c,u_j)=B(u_c,v_j)-\sum _{i<j} rac{B(u_i,v_j)}{B(u_i,u_i)}B(u_c,u_i). \]

Orthogonality kills every summand except $i=c$, and that term cancels $B(u_c,v_j)$.

□
